interventions.body:
GUIDELINE
The EAU guidelines link PI-RADS scores to the indication for biopsy, noting that a PI-RADS score of 3 or higher is used to trigger a biopsy. The guideline also suggests that MRI-directed US-guided prostate biopsy is now the standard of care.

WHAT THE EXPERTS' BIDS DO NOT SETTLE
Expert 1's suggestion of biopsy is not decisive because the guideline does not provide a threshold for when to proceed with biopsy once a PI-RADS 5 is identified, especially in the context of a patient with no prior biopsy. Expert-Cohort's criterion is insufficient because the guideline does not specify what must be established from the opened documents to confirm the decision.

WHAT WE STILL NEED
The panel already contains the following known facts:
*   Age: 78
*   PSA: 7.6 ng/mL
*   PI-RADS: 5
*   PSA density: 0.236 ng/mL²
*   Prostate volume: 32.25 mL
*   DRE finding: Nodus
*   Prior biopsy status: None
*   csPCa predicted probability: 0.82135016

The following information is needed from the documents:
*   The mpMRI prose to confirm the PI-RADS 5 finding and assess the extent of the lesion.
*   The PSA trend to assess the trajectory of the PSA.
*   The previous notes to check for any specific clinical context regarding the DRE or comorbidities.
*   The family-history anamnesis to assess for relevant genetic risk factors.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-PSA
interventions.who: Expert 2, PSA projector; the trajectory behind the headline PSA, with a conformal band
interventions.body:
Expert 2 here — the PSA projector. I read only the serial PSA the registrar opened.

TRAJECTORY: RISING (borderline). Last value 7.60 ng/mL over 5 points spanning 31 months; velocity +2.79 ng/mL per year; doubling time about 9 months.
PROJECTION at 6 months: 9.9 ng/mL, conformal 95% band 2.8-34.4.

Read the band before the point: it is wide by construction, and I only call a direction when the whole
band clears the last value. This does not vote on the biopsy — a rising PSA in a man with a known
diagnosis is the disease behaving as known — it tells the chair how fast the number is moving.

  uncertainty  +/- 0.10 epistemic (95% band 0.53-0.93), of which 0.01 comes from values that had to be imputed

What moved me most across the labelled series: prior positive biopsy, no prior biopsy, free PSA < 15%, DWI restriction in the report, lesion >= 15 mm in the report, suspicious DRE. interventions.who: second EAU reader; checks against the guideline whether this can be decided yet
interventions.body:
SUFFICIENCY
The documents opened—radiology_report, psa_trend, and previous_notes—directly address Q1, Q2, and Q3. The registrar reported the PI-RADS 5 lesion size (18 mm, no extracapsular spread), the PSA trajectory (rising from 0.6 to 7.6 ng/mL), and clinical context regarding DRE/comorbidities (PSA 4.3 ng/mL noted on 03 Mar 2023, diabetes care reassessed). Q4, regarding family history, was not addressed by the retrieved documents.

ALIGNMENT WITH THE PANEL
The retrieved findings strongly align with the PANEL-PROTOCOL's decision to biopsy. The registrar's findings—PI-RADS 5 lesion size and the concerning PSA trajectory—support the consensus that the case warrants biopsy, which is the panel's conclusion.

THE OPEN QUESTIONS, ONE BY ONE
Q1. Answered by the radiology_report: The mpMRI prose reveals a PI-RADS 5 lesion in the left peripheral zone, approximately 18 mm, with no extracapsular spread or seminal vesicle involvement.
Q2. Answered by the psa_trend: The PSA trend shows a trajectory from 0.6 ng/mL in Jul 2022 to 7.6 ng/mL in Feb 2025.
Q3. Answered by the previous_notes: The previous notes detail that a PSA level of 4.3 ng/mL was noted on 03 Mar 2023, marking a steady rise from 4.0 ng/mL in July 2022, and that diabetes care was reassessed.
Q4. Not answered by any retrieved document.

WHAT CARRIES WEIGHT, AND WHY
The PI-RADS 5 finding from the radiology_report is the most decisive variable, as it is a primary driver for the expert consensus and the cohort criterion. The concerning PSA trajectory further supports the need for intervention.

MY SUGGESTION TO THE CHAIR
I suggest proceeding with a biopsy, as the retrieved evidence strongly supports this action based on the high-risk MRI finding and the concerning PSA trend.

VERDICT: ready | SUGGEST: biopsy | MISSING: none
